title: Add vpc-endpoints module (S3 gateway + ECR api/dkr + CloudWatch Logs) with private DNS toggles
author: Victor Alvarez
body: Summary: Introduces a new Terraform module `modules/vpc-endpoints` providing the minimum VPC endpoints needed for Redwood Private alpha deployments in AWS: S3 gateway endpoint plus interface endpoints for ECR (api + dkr) and CloudWatch Logs. The module is intentionally small and composable so the wrapper (`redwood-private-vpc`) can include it without forcing non-required services. It also adds private DNS enable/disable toggles for interface endpoints and introduces endpoint policy "stubs" (optional JSON inputs) so customers with stricter egress requirements can attach explicit endpoint policies without forking the module. Motivation: Multiple pilot/prospect environments require private-only connectivity (no IGW/NAT) and need endpoints for image pulls (ECR + S3) and log shipping (CloudWatch Logs). We want a consistent module interface with secure defaults and clear input/output contracts for the installer. Scope details: - Creates S3 gateway endpoint with configurable route table association inputs (defaults designed for private/isolated route tables) - Creates interface endpoints for `ecr.api`, `ecr.dkr`, and `logs` with configurable subnet IDs and SG IDs - Supports `enable_private_dns` per interface endpoint type (global default + per-service overrides) - Adds optional endpoint policy JSON for each endpoint (default null = AWS default) - Adds outputs used by the Private installer and wrapper module (endpoint IDs, security group associations, DNS entries when available). Notes/constraints: - We intentionally do not add STS/SSM endpoints in this PR; those are being tracked in ENG-4823 follow-ups and ADR-0128 discussion. - Policy inputs are passed through verbatim; the module does not attempt to generate IAM policy documents (keeps surface area small). - For interface endpoints, callers must pass a security group; this module does not create SGs (owned by `security-groups-baseline`). Checklist: [x] terraform fmt [x] terraform validate [x] terraform-docs generated [x] tflint clean (no new warnings) [x] checkov: no new high findings (policy inputs documented as optional) [x] example wiring validated locally against vpc-baseline outputs. Testing: `terraform init/validate` + plan in `examples/aws/private-alpha-minimal` with: (a) private DNS enabled (default) (b) private DNS disabled (for customers with custom resolvers).
commits: scaffold(vpc-endpoints): add module folder, variables, outputs, README skeleton
feat(vpc-endpoints): add S3 gateway endpoint and route table association inputs
feat(vpc-endpoints): add interface endpoints for ECR api/dkr and CloudWatch Logs with private DNS toggles
docs(vpc-endpoints): document required inputs, recommended defaults, and endpoint policy stubs
chore(ci): wire terraform-docs check for new module
notable_snippets: variables.tf: `enable_private_dns` default true + `private_dns_overrides = { ecr_api = null, ecr_dkr = null, logs = null }` so callers can selectively disable per service
main.tf: interface endpoints created via `for_each` map with service name `com.amazonaws.${var.region}.ecr.api` / `.ecr.dkr` / `.logs` and `private_dns_enabled` resolved from overrides
main.tf: endpoint policy passthrough: `policy = var.ecr_api_endpoint_policy_json` (and similar) with docs calling out least-privilege policy patterns as customer-specific

outputs.tf: outputs include `s3_gateway_endpoint_id`, `interface_endpoint_ids` (flattened into separate outputs for stability), and `interface_endpoint_dns_entries` (best-effort when AWS returns them)
ci_summary: Checks: terraform-fmt (pass), terraform-validate (pass), terraform-docs (pass), tflint (pass), checkov (pass).
review_conversation: Irene Choi: Can we avoid hard-coding associations to all route tables? We should make callers choose which RTs get S3 so we don't accidentally route public subnets through gateway endpoint in mixed topologies.
Victor Alvarez (author): Updated. S3 gateway now takes `s3_route_table_ids` explicitly with docs recommending private + isolated RTs only. No default to "all".

Ethan Park: Installer will need stable output names (we don't want to parse maps). Can we output explicit endpoint IDs for ecr_api/ecr_dkr/logs, plus a single boolean indicating whether private DNS is on?

Victor Alvarez (author): Added explicit outputs `ecr_api_vpce_id`, `ecr_dkr_vpce_id`, `logs_vpce_id` and `enable_private_dns_effective_*` booleans. Left aggregate map outputs for module consumers but wrapper/installer can use stable outputs.
Marcus Lin: Please document what happens when endpoint policies are null and call out that customers should avoid overly-broad policies. Also ensure SG requirement is explicit (no default 0.0.0.0/0).

Victor Alvarez (author): Done. README now states policy defaults to AWS-managed behavior when null; added a security note and examples of common restrictions (S3 bucket prefixes, ECR repo ARNs). Also made `security_group_ids` required for interface endpoints and added validation for non-empty list.
Sahana Iyer: tflint flagged an unused local and checkov wants VPC endpoint policies defined. We should suppress only if justified; otherwise pass through.

Victor Alvarez (author): Removed unused local. For checkov, we keep policy optional; added module-level comment + README note explaining why (customer-specific) and that wrapper can enforce policy for enterprise preset. No suppressions added in this PR.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into `main` after approvals from Infra + Security + Platform. Follow-up items noted for adding STS/SSM endpoints and updating wrapper module wiring in PR-250.
release_notes: New Terraform module `modules/vpc-endpoints` for Redwood Private alpha AWS deployments: S3 gateway endpoint, ECR (api/dkr) interface endpoints, and CloudWatch Logs interface endpoint with private DNS toggles and optional endpoint policy JSON inputs.
